claim_checks.claim: `private` and `protected` are enforced only during type checking. Runtime lookups, and bracket notation even during type checking, still reach the member: it is "soft private".
claim_checks.page_says: private and protected are only enforced during type checking ... private also allows access using bracket notation during type checking ... these fields are soft private
claim_checks.note: Runtime access to private and protected members is supported. The page attributes bracket-notation access during type checking, and the label 'soft private', to private only; the claim's 'the member' extends both to protected members (wider scope).

claim_checks.claim: `#` fields stay private after compilation and have no bracket-notation escape hatch: they are "hard private".
claim_checks.page_says: JavaScript’s private fields (#) remain private after compilation and do not provide the previously mentioned escape hatches like bracket notation access, making them hard private.

claim_checks.claim: When compiling to ES2021 or lower, TypeScript replaces `#` with `WeakMap`s. The handbook notes that these runtime privacy checks will degrade performance.
claim_checks.page_says: When compiling to ES2021 or less, TypeScript will use WeakMaps in place of #. ... Note that these added privacy checks during runtime could affect performance.
claim_checks.note: The WeakMap downlevel part is supported. The handbook says the checks 'could affect' performance, and says it of hard-privacy mechanisms in general (closures, WeakMaps, private fields); the claim raises this to 'will degrade' (MUST-level modal) and ties it to the downlevelled WeakMaps.

claim_checks.claim: Private elements are not properties. They cannot be enumerated, deleted, proxied, or reached through `Object` methods, and `structuredClone()` copies them like public fields.
claim_checks.page_says: they cannot be proxied, enumerated, deleted, or interacted with using any Object method. ... For this reason, structuredClone() does not clone private elements
claim_checks.note: The first sentence and the list are supported. The structuredClone() part inverts the page: MDN says structuredClone() does not clone private elements.

claim_checks.claim: Reading a `#` field from an object whose class did not declare it throws a `TypeError`. `#x in obj` checks for it without throwing.
claim_checks.page_says: from an object that doesn't have the element, a TypeError is thrown ... use the in operator to check whether an externally defined object possesses a private element
claim_checks.note: The page's example error reads 'Cannot read private member #x from an object whose class did not declare it'; the in check returns true or false.

claim_checks.claim: V8 9.4 moved class-field initialization, including private fields, onto its inline-cache fast path. Before that it went through slower runtime calls.
claim_checks.page_says: The first issue has been fixed in V8 v9.7 ... Before v9.7, V8 always used a costly runtime call for class field initializations.
claim_checks.note: Wrong version: the page gives v9.7, not 9.4 (the doc's own applies-to also says V8 >= 9.7). The claim also drops the condition that the IC is used only 'when V8 considers the pattern of the initialization to be predictable enough', with a runtime-call fallback otherwise.

claim_checks.claim: An injected collaborator (port, clock, logger) | `private readonly x` constructor parameter | A `#` name cannot be a parameter property
claim_checks.page_says: Allow `#`-private names in parameter property positions ... That this is not possible is a bit surprising
claim_checks.note: The issue (a feature request) supports the statement, but the source is Rank 6 cited in a role 3 section; recorded separately as a KB-15 breach.

claim_checks.claim: Object wrapped in a `Proxy` (some mocking and reactivity libraries) | `#` access does not go through the proxy | Private elements cannot be proxied
claim_checks.page_says: they cannot be proxied, enumerated, deleted, or interacted with using any Object method.

claim_checks.claim: Target ES2021 or lower | `#` becomes `WeakMap` lookups | TypeScript downlevels it
claim_checks.page_says: When compiling to ES2021 or less, TypeScript will use WeakMaps in place of #.

claim_checks.claim: Working around it with `--experimental-transform-types` | ... the flag is removed in Node 26.0.0 | So code meant to run unbuilt keeps injected collaborators as `readonly #field`s assigned in the constructor
claim_checks.page_says: Removed --experimental-transform-types flag. (v26.0.0 row) ... any TypeScript features that involve replacing TypeScript syntax with new JavaScript syntax will error ... parameter properties
claim_checks.note: The Node 24.22 ExperimentalWarning run is labelled as a local re-test and was not grounded against the page.

claim_checks.claim: Type stripping itself | Stable (stability 2) since Node 24.12.0 and 25.2.0; no warning since 24.3.0; Node ignores `tsconfig.json` and needs `.ts` extensions in relative imports | Node only deletes types
claim_checks.page_says: Type stripping is now stable. ... Stability: 2 - Stable ... no longer emits an experimental warning. ... Node.js ignores tsconfig.json files ... file extensions are mandatory in import statements
claim_checks.note: History table rows: v25.2.0, v24.12.0 stable; v24.3.0, v22.18.0 no experimental warning.

conflicts.topic: structuredClone() and private elements: How it works step 4 says they are copied; the cited MDN page says they are not (counted once, as grounding finding C4)
V8 version of the class-field inline-cache fix: How it works step 6 says 9.4; the cited V8 blog and the doc's own applies-to say 9.7 (counted once, as grounding finding C6)

violations.evidence: C3: step 3 says the handbook notes runtime privacy checks 'will degrade performance'; the handbook says 'these added privacy checks during runtime could affect performance', about hard-privacy mechanisms in general.
C4: step 4 says structuredClone() copies private elements like public fields; MDN says 'structuredClone() does not clone private elements'.

C6: step 6 says V8 9.4; the V8 blog says 'The first issue has been fixed in V8 v9.7' and 'Before v9.7, V8 always used a costly runtime call'. The fast-path condition (predictable initialization pattern) is also dropped.
The 'Where each form fits' table under How it works (role 3, allowed ranks 1-4) cites [^5], a GitHub issue (Rank 6), for 'A # name cannot be a parameter property'.

C1: step 1 extends bracket-notation access during type checking and the 'soft private' label to protected members; the handbook states both for private only ('private also allows access using bracket notation during type checking').
[^6] (TC39 class fields proposal) is listed as backing 'How it works 2' but is never cited in the body; step 2 cites only [^1].
States 'Verified: 10 claims (✅)', but the body carries 11 ✅ marks (How it works 1-6, the Where each form fits row, and four Edge cases rows).

'On a native ES2022+ target, reading and creating # fields costs the same as public fields' (and the Takeaways 'measured cost is nil') is unmarked and uncited, and generalizes to every engine from one local V8 13.6 measurement; [^3] limits the fast path to V8 v9.7+ and to predictable initialization patterns.

No section does the work of role 2 (concept architecture) or role 5 (reference & invariants). Exact reference values (stability levels, version history) sit in Edge cases, and the 'Where each form fits' design-guidance table sits inside the mechanism section.
